thesis: Navan (NAVN) closed at $27.20, about 11% below its Aug 27 close ($30.58) but well above its 200-day average ($19.28) and about 12% under its 52-week high ($30.88). The main company-specific event is the Sept 9 fiscal Q2 2027 report (revenue about $232.8M, +35% YoY, with guidance reported as raised), after which the stock dropped sharply to ~$20 and has since recovered to ~$27. Secondary sources conflict on whether the print was a beat or a miss, so the read on the results is not fully resolved, and the catalyst is older than 15 trading days; no primary release was retrieved this run. Counter-case: a plaintiff-side IPO securities class action (class period Oct 28, 2025-Feb 23, 2026; lead-plaintiff deadline Apr 24, 2026 already passed) and a June 2026 derivative-claim investigation exist, but no scheduled ruling, hearing or deadline within ~90 days was found, and no restatement, auditor change or indictment turned up, so no risk flag. Next earnings reported as Dec 14-16, 2026. This suggests a medium-conviction long setup based on recovery from the post-earnings drop rather than a fresh catalyst.
invalidation: Guidance cut or further margin deterioration at the next report, a close below the 200-day average, or a scheduled adverse ruling or new governance event in the IPO litigation.
